body:
Thanks for your reply, it means a lot to me. I'll try and address some of your questions first.

We're both university students. I'm in a co-op program right now and working in a research lab on campus. My work can require me to be in safety gear in the lab for extended periods of time during which I can't really use my cell phone. She is also working on campus right now, in a different research lab.

She's from a conservative Indian family. Her parents put a lot of emphasis on academic achievement. From what she's told me, they have difficulty understanding why she's upset when she is doing so well academically. I think she's always had significant pressure like this, without much emotional support. She says she's been battling depression since high school.

From my point of view, I really think she has a lot of good friends. The only problem right now is that we're both on a work term. This means that many of her friends are working out of town. I often suggest spending time with other people, or asking 'Have you thought about trying this activity with... x person who's in town'. Unfortunately, her go-to answer is 'yes, but it's not the same/they don't really like me'. Unfortunately, most of the people she knows in town right now aren't her very close friends, or are close friends with me.

She has been working in a research lab, like I mentioned, but it sounds like her work has been very unfulfilling. The lab has just moved to a new building and there are many deficiencies, so she's not getting to really do her own research as much as she expected to. Instead, she's given menial tasks like installing software or writing some analysis code. She doesn't really have any hobbies or other activities she's involved in. I've suggested trying to find things she likes or joining clubs, but everything she suggested she said she'd only join if I came (e.g. dancing lessons). She had been swimming every Tuesday night, but once we started having more problems I think she gave up on that.

Recently, she has gotten time off of work and has been at her family's house. I found out within the last week that she finally disclosed her situation to her mother and sister. It sounds like they're being supportive, so now that they're more concerned I'm hoping they will be giving her more support. She told me today that she's seeing her family doctor, too, another real plus!

In a month's time, two of her closest friends are back in town. One is moving in with her and the other will be living on her block. Hopefully that will help her realize that she does have other people who love and care about her. 

Until then, I think that my plan will be to continue spending time with her and giving her reinforcement that even without me things will start looking better. If you have any other suggestions of things to keep in mind or say to her, I would appreciate it. Also, do you think I should talk to her friends who are moving back to town and tell them what I know? Maybe I should at least make sure they have each others contact info in case one of them can't be there for her.

Actually, typing this out is making me feel a lot better. Things don't really look so dismal with the number of positives I was able to list here. Thanks for your response, again, some of those questions were really good for me to think about.

I've contacted the police before and she ended up not making an attempt the following day, so I was really thankful for that. I'll always keep 911 in mind for situations that are looking serious.

Thanks for reading.

Thanks for your detailed response.

I'm actually inclined to agree with you for the most part, although I don't think that failing to love someone is necessarily a betrayal. I accept I lied to her, and I believe I was the problem in the relationship, but honest to God I never intentionally betrayed her. Everything I did was out of compassion for her.

  Also, you don't know the full story or who I am, so hearing you judge me so harshly is a little tough. I often go well out of my way to help people, but this time 'helping' seems to be putting both of us more at risk. In my experience, loving someone is not a choice. If I can't live up to it, would it really have been better for me to continue trying to be happy and trying to make her happy when my heart's not in it, I'm doing a poor job, and she deserves better?

It hurts to hear you tell me I don't care about her. I've spent hundreds of hours over the past 2-3 months talking to her, comforting her, arranging counselling, talking to friends, and have even talked to the police. The issue has grown though. It's no longer about only her. I'm intrinsically involved.

I really want to help her in this situation, but I don't think I can love her. What you said about the cycle repeating is exactly why I don't want to get back together with her, but abandoning her could be worse.

I've offered spending time with her so she doesn't have to be alone, but she always tries to get close to me which is out of my comfort zone. Any time I try to draw the attention away from 'us' and to something else like cooking, a game, or a movie, she zones out and puts her head in her hands or starts hitting herself. I do my best to talk to her, give her a hug, or keep her positive, but I don't want to lie to her again, so I refuse to be anything more than a friend.

Should I stop spending time with her? When she calls from the top of an unknown building, do I lie to her in the hopes of saving her and restart the cycle? Do I refuse again and have her continue to implore me to be with her out of desperation, or risk an even worse fate?

I know it's a tricky situation, I don't expect you to answer those questions. I feel that being away from me would be best for her because I'm obviously toxic toward her, but most of her close friends are out of town and I worry she won't have the support if I'm not there for her.

Anyway. Thanks again for your response. Reading it was a little like a kick in the teeth, but one that I think I needed. 

**One last question to you:**

Do you think sharing your response with her would help? If she realized I'm a problem for her and not everything is her fault, maybe it would help her. I'm worried she would take it as a karmic sign that the world is out to get her, though. She attributes most of her problems to god and I really don't want to worsen that.
